query: For high-entropy alloys, what single intervention could improve hardness and strength without sacrificing useful mechanical performance? Formulate one hypothesis that specifies the intervention, the mechanism expected to produce the improvement, a measurable outcome relative to an untreated baseline, the conditions under which the hypothesis should hold, prior evidence supporting it, and an experiment with clear observations that would falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: The addition of Zr to high-entropy alloys can improve hardness and strength without sacrificing useful mechanical performance.
generation.material_initial_state: High-entropy alloy in its as-cast state
generation.intervention: Addition of Zr to the alloy composition
generation.conditions: The alloy is subjected to thermomechanical treatment, including hot rolling and annealing
generation.structural_mediator: Solid solution strengthening due to the large atomic radius of Zr
generation.mechanism: The addition of Zr leads to an increase in grain size and a refinement of grain boundaries, resulting in improved mechanical properties
generation.predicted_outcome: Improved yield strength and ductility, with a potential increase in specific yield strength
generation.baseline: The mechanical properties of the high-entropy alloy without Zr addition
generation.boundary: The optimal composition and processing conditions for the Zr-added high-entropy alloy
generation.uncertainty: The exact mechanism by which Zr addition improves mechanical properties, and the potential effects of other alloying elements

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare a series of high-entropy alloys with varying Zr content, and subject them to thermomechanical treatment
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the addition of Zr does not lead to an improvement in yield strength and ductility, the hypothesis is falsified

Efficient production of a high-performance dispersion strengthened, multi-principal element alloy

Abstract: Additive manufacturing currently facilitates new avenues for materials discovery that have not been fully explored. In this study we reveal how additive manufacturing can be leveraged to produce dispersion strengthened (DS), multi-principal element alloys (MPEA) without the use of traditional mechanical alloying or chemical reactions. This new processing technique employed resonant acoustic mixing to coat an equiatomic NiCoCr powder with nano-scale yttrium oxides. Then, through laser powder bed fusion (L-PBF), the coated powder was successfully consolidated into 99.9% dense parts. Microstructural analysis confirmed the successful incorporation and dispersion of nano-scale oxides throughout the build volume. Furthermore, high temperature mechanical testing of the DS alloys showed significant improvements in strength and ductility over the baseline NiCoCr. Remarkable Enhanced Mechanical Properties of TiAlCrNbV Medium-Entropy Alloy with Zr Additions

Abstract: Most medium entropy alloys (MEAs) exhibit excellent mechanical properties, but their applications are limited because of their high density. This study explores a series of lightweight nonequiatomic Ti65(AlCrNbV)35-xZrx (x = 3, 5, 7, and 10) MEAs with a low density, high strength, and high ductility. To achieve solid solution strengthening, Zr with a large atomic radius was used. In addition, various thermomechanical treatment parameters were adopted to further improve the MEAs’ mechanical properties. The density of the MEAs was revealed to be approximately 5 g/cm3, indicating that they were lightweight. Through an X-ray diffraction analysis, the MEAs were revealed to have a single body-centered cubic structure not only in the as-cast state but also after thermomechanical treatment. In terms of mechanical properties, all the as-cast MEAs with Zr additions achieved excellent performance (>1000 MPa tensile yield strength and 20% tensile ductility).
